reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's risk-off call (SPY 715.87, 1.96% under its 200-day, 20d realized vol 23.7%, every sector SPDR down over 5d), though his confidence is only 0.45 because credit has not cracked. Checking every holding from its stop block and stored clauses (L7): the shared VOO/VTI stop is TRIPPED and the RSP clause is met again and worse (RSP 21d -2.31%), so I approve P1 and P2 together as one exit, about 23.1% of equity on one line, keeping the 11-17 pre-commitment (L9). FAST's 'marginal hold if XLI keeps lagging' condition is met (the Skeptic is right that XLI is 6.59% below its 200-day per market.json, not the stale 4.70%), Industrials is avoided and the Proposer delivered the sale owed under L8, so P3 is approved. EXEL is NEAR (+1.3%) and its stored favored-sector premise is gone, so P4 is approved; I take the Skeptic's point that the lost Health Care premise falls hardest on IDXX (8.1% of equity, beta 0.80), but I cannot originate a trim, so I pick EXEL first for the INCY oncology overlap and F7 vs IDXX's F8, restate IDXX's and INCY's premises through thesis_updates today (L8), and name IDXX the next trim candidate: the Proposer owes a trim proposal or an explicit hold verdict on it at the next run. P5 (TLT) is resized from $40 to $25: the Skeptic's serious objection holds, because TLT is chosen only since IEF and BND are wash-sale blocked, the duration-hedging evidence is one week old, it reverses the IEF/BND sales of a week ago and the 12-09 FOMC sits inside its test window; the Market Analyst does prefer Treasuries today, so a smaller ticket follows his call without reversing it (L4). TLT tracks 20+ year Treasuries and IEF 7-10 year, so I judge it not substantially identical to the blocked IEF (Implicator's flag); its qualitative clause is restated as a measurable 5-day test (L6). Other holdings: CARG, DPZ, MSCI, VRSN, KR, SAM, INCY, IDXX and WMT have no tripped price stop or qualitative clause; WMT's XLP 21d is +3.16%, above +3%, and I accept the Skeptic's point that 'while SPY holds' silences the clause in a falling market, so it is restated without that condition; KR's baby-food report is not its cyber clause; SAM's founder-CEO handover (8-K 5.02) is a planned internal succession with no guidance change and is written into the thesis. Event dates (L2): no holding reports within 5 sessions; KR's company-confirmed 12-03 call is the nearest. After the trades about $256 (about 42%) is cash: that cash is idled by the regime filter (only BND, GLD, IEF, TLT buyable; BND and IEF blocked, GLD rejected by the Market Analyst as not hedging), not by choice, and it is not a reason to keep any invalidated position (L4). Re-entry plan, answering the Skeptic on P2: when SPY closes back above its 200-day, deploy first into single names with their own stops in the Market Analyst's favored sectors, sized against buckets (Staples is already 16.5%, so Utilities or other non-stacked quality names come first), and only rebuy VOO or VTI after their wash-sale windows end about 12-20; QQQ is not the re-entry vehicle while Technology is the worst sector.
